Connect the dots
The all-inclusive gym wave: blueprint or warning shot?
The all-inclusive model — one price, every service, zero friction — isn't a European quirk. It's a structural bet that members will pay more when they stop doing math at the door. body LIFE is reporting it's actively reshaping gym expansion strategy across Europe, and the operators paying attention aren't waiting for it to cross borders before they stress-test their own pricing architecture.
The concrete 'so what': if your studio still sells à la carte add-ons (nutrition, recovery, programming), you're asking members to make a buying decision every single time. The all-inclusive playbook removes that resistance by design. This week's question isn't whether to go all-in — it's whether your current offer can compete when a bundled competitor opens two blocks away.
The rundown
01
All-Inclusive Fitness Is Expanding — Here's What Studio Ops Need to Know
The fitness market is seeing a push toward all-inclusive models, and body LIFE has the intel studio operators need to stay ahead. Consider this your cheat sheet.
Source: body LIFE →
02
SuperMush Bags $3M to Fuel Its Wellness Expansion
Wellness brand SuperMush has raised $3 million from NDude to grow its product lineup. Mushrooms, money, and momentum — what a combo.
Source: Indian Startup News →
03
Longevity Movement Is Leaving Women Behind, Experts Say
The longevity boom has a women problem, according to experts cited by Athletech News. Turns out living forever is complicated when half the population feels left out of the conversation.
Source: Athletech News →
04
Garmin's Golf Watch Looks the Part but Misses the Fairway
TechRadar put Garmin's Approach S72 through its paces — promising everything golfers and smartwatch fans could want, it still didn't quite deliver the golf watch the reviewer craved.
Source: TechRadar →
05
Smart Glasses Are Coming for Your Gym Routine
DSSV is reporting on smart glasses making their way into the fitness studio. We don't know exactly what they do there, but they're watching.
Source: DSSV →
06
10 Grants to Bring Exercise Programs to Cancer Patients
HFA and the American Cancer Society are funding 10 grants to expand fitness programming for people affected by cancer — proof that the industry's reach goes well beyond the weight room, and a signal for operators that oncology fitness is a lane worth watching.
Source: Health & Fitness Association →
Stat
10
grants funded by HFA and the American Cancer Society for oncology fitness programs
Ten grants is a small number with a large signal — institutional money is formally recognising oncology fitness as a programming category, which means studios ignoring it are behind a curve that's already funded.

✓ Steal: Borrow the hotel industry's 'all-inclusive upsell audit' tactic: list every service a competitor could bundle that you currently charge separately for, then rank each by margin and member demand.

Connect the dots
Big-box money can't buy what you already have
When a franchise drops $100 million on expansion, the instinct is to panic. Don't. Scale is a blunt instrument — it multiplies locations, not relationships. Every new cookie-cutter box that opens near you is also a billboard reminding locals that something more personal exists. The operators who win the next five years won't out-spend the giants; they'll out-know their members in ways no franchise playbook can replicate.
So this week's move isn't defensive — it's offensive. Audit what your big-box competitor literally cannot offer: your coach's name on a check-in text, the program adjustment made because you remembered someone's knee surgery, the community that shows up when someone's having a rough month. These aren't soft perks. They're structural moats. Document them, market them explicitly, and price accordingly — because the franchise wave doesn't kill differentiated studios, it culls the ones that forgot to differentiate.
The rundown
01
Italy Leads the 2026 World Spa Awards — and Spas Are Leveling Up
World Spa Awards 2026 has crowned Italy the one to beat, while the industry signals spas are evolving well beyond hot stones and herbal wraps. If you run recovery or wellness programming, the bar just got a lot more interesting.
Source: Luxus Plus →
02
GLORIAH Pulls In £600K to Grow Its Intimate Wellness Brand
The UK-based intimate wellness company has closed a £600K raise, per Femtech Insider — a reminder that the wellness economy keeps expanding well beyond the gym floor, and operators ignoring adjacent categories may be leaving real money on the table.
Source: Femtech Insider →
03
£184m NHS deal crowns world's first reusable ECG wearable
Cambridge Heartwear just landed a £184m NHS contract for a reusable ECG wearable — meaning heart-rate monitoring is getting a serious upgrade that coaches and studio operators will want on their radar as client wellness tech goes clinical-grade.
Source: NottinghamWorld →
04
Up to $250 Off Hyperice Gear This Fall Prime Day
Hyperice is running a Fall Prime Day sale with up to $250 off its pro athlete-favorite recovery tools — meaning your clients' favorite excuse ('I can't afford a Hypervolt') just got a lot harder to make.
Source: Athletech News →
05
SuperMush banks $3M to grow its functional wellness line
The mushroom-forward brand just closed a $3M Series A — worth watching if you're thinking about what's sitting on your studio's retail shelf.
Source: Dealroom →
06
$100m expansion plan puts gym franchise in serious growth mode
A gym franchise is flexing hard with a $100 million expansion push — which means more locations, more competition, and more reason for independent operators to double down on what big boxes can't replicate.
Source: 1News →
Sqwod recs
✓ Steal: Run a 'member intelligence' sprint: pull your last 30 check-in notes or PT session logs and tag the three most common non-fitness themes (stress, sleep, life events). Build one touchpoint this month that speaks directly to the top theme — it's the personalization big boxes can't automate.
✓ Try: Introduce a 'recovery office hours' slot — 20 minutes, no workout, just a coach reviewing a member's sleep, HRV, or soreness patterns. Low overhead, high perceived value, and a direct counter-positioning move against volume-first competitors.

item.description: Hot products sell out — and so does your credibility when you've already promised members something you can't deliver.
item.content:encoded:
Thursday, 01 October 2026 View online →
DAILY
The fitness industry, decoded — in five minutes.

— Sqwod
Money movement
⇄  Acquired
McDonald's

Connect the dots
Viral fitness gear + your calendar = a hidden risk
Whoop's marketing machine worked almost too well: demand spiked faster than inventory could follow, leaving gaps that no amount of brand heat could paper over. For a wearables company that's one thing — for a studio operator who's built a 6-week program around a specific device or product, it's a class cancellation, a refund conversation, and a trust dent you didn't budget for.
The move: audit your next quarter's programming now for any single points of product failure — a wearable, a supplement partner, a piece of kit that's 'assumed available.' Build a 2-week buffer into your launch timeline and have a named backup. Supply chain risk isn't just a logistics problem; when your programming calendar is the product, it's a retention problem.
The rundown
01
Whoop's Marketing Glow-Up Created a Supply Chain Headache
Whoop's pivot to aggressive marketing fueled hypergrowth — but also exposed serious demand planning gaps. If you're betting on a hot fitness product to stay in stock, this is your reminder to build buffer into your programming calendar.
Source: Chief Marketer →
02
The Business Case for Taking Your Fitness Community on the Road
Athletech News makes the case for mobile fitness experiences as a legit growth lever — if you've ever thought about popping up somewhere new, this is your sign to run the numbers first.
Source: Athletech News →
03
$24K in 24 Hours: A Gym Shows Up for an Injured Member
A San Diego gym rallied its community to raise $24,000 in a single day for a woman hurt by a fleeing Tesla — a reminder that your studio's most powerful asset isn't its equipment, it's the room's willingness to show up.
Source: cbs8.com →
04
DSSV Webinar: Copyright & Trademark Law for Your Studio
The DSSV is hosting an online legal seminar on copyright and trademark law specifically for fitness studios — because knowing your rights is just as important as knowing your reps.
Source: DSSV →
05
McDonald's is dropping $8.5B to reinvent itself for the Ozempic era
The Golden Arches is betting $8.5 billion on a leaner, post-GLP-1 menu future — and while investors are skeptical of the price tag, it's a loud signal that even fast food knows the appetite for 'eat less' is very, very real.
Source: moneywise.com →
Policy watch
Copyright & Trademark Law Is Coming to Your Studio
The DSSV is hosting an online legal seminar covering copyright and trademark law specifically for fitness studios — the kind of protection most operators skip until it's expensive not to. If your brand name, class formats, or content aren't formally protected, this is the cheapest insurance you'll find this quarter.
Sqwod recs
✓ Track: Start logging your month-over-month member retention rate by cohort (join month) — most studios watch total headcount and miss the slow leak hiding in months 3–5.
✓ Steal: Run a 'community credit' system: members who refer, volunteer, or show up for a studio event earn a small account credit — turns goodwill into a measurable loyalty loop.
✓ Try: Block one hour this month to do a 'brand audit' of your studio's name, logo, and any signature class names — search trademark databases (e.g. USPTO or your country's equivalent) before someone else files first.

Connect the dots
Your machines are generating data you're not selling yet
IPercept's $16.5M raise isn't really about sensors — it's about the moment operators realized that utilization data, maintenance prediction, and member-engagement signals were sitting inside their equipment doing absolutely nothing. Every rep logged, every machine left idle at 6pm, every cable stack that spikes in March and dies in June is a business insight dressed as a hardware problem. The investors writing those checks aren't betting on Bluetooth — they're betting that the gap between 'we have machines' and 'we understand how our members use them' is worth serious money to close.
So what does that mean if you run a studio with twelve pieces of kit and no enterprise software budget? It means the question to ask your next equipment vendor isn't 'what's the warranty' — it's 'what data does this export, and where does it go.' Operators who start building that habit now, even manually with a simple utilization log, will have the baseline that actually makes smart tracking tools useful when they arrive. The infrastructure is coming. The data habit is the moat.

Connect the dots
The beauty-wellness merger isn't a trend — it's a land grab
Amaani just pulled in $5M led by BECO Capital to scale a brand sitting squarely at the intersection of beauty and wellness. That's not a niche raise — that's investors betting that consumers no longer separate 'feeling good' from 'looking good.' The spa menu, the skin-health consultation, the recovery ritual: these aren't add-ons anymore, they're the category.
For studio operators, the so-what is this: your four walls of treadmills and kettlebells are competing against experiences that address the whole self. You don't need a skincare line — but you do need to audit whether your client journey ends at the workout or extends into recovery, ritual, and results they can see. The studios that figure this out first won't just retain clients longer; they'll command higher ticket prices.
The rundown
01
Amaani pulls in $5M to grow its beauty & wellness play
The BECO Capital-led raise signals serious investor appetite for beauty-meets-wellness brands — worth noting if you're a studio owner wondering whether 'spa services' belong on your menu.

$10.1B: WHOOP Just Got a Ronaldo-Sized Vote of Confidence
Cristiano Ronaldo has made a multi-million dollar investment in WHOOP, pushing the sports tech brand to a $10.1 billion valuation. If the world's most data-obsessed athlete is putting money where his metrics are, it's worth asking whether wearable tech is moving from nice-to-have to non-negotiable in your client offering.
Source: Sportscape Magazine →
03
The Picklr Is Cutting Staff and 'Evaluating Options'
The fast-growing pickleball franchise is hitting a rough patch, with layoffs and an uncertain road ahead. If you've been watching the franchise fitness space, this is a good reminder that hypergrowth and sustainable operations aren't always playing the same game.
Source: Athletech News →
04
5 Home Exercises That Burn Fat and Build Muscle
Hindustan Times rounded up a fitness coach's five go-to home workout moves for burning fat and building muscle — handy intel if your clients keep canceling their gym memberships but still want results.
Source: Hindustan Times →
05
£500 raised: Welwyn Garden City gym event backs Willow
A local fitness fundraiser cleared £500 for Willow — proof that when studios rally a community around a cause, the numbers (and the goodwill) add up fast.
Source: Welwyn Hatfield Times →

Oura Ring 5 review: Is it still top of the stack?
220 Triathlon put the Oura Ring 5 through its paces to answer the question every wearable-curious coach is asking. If you're advising athletes on recovery tracking, this is worth a read before you make a recommendation.

item.content:encoded:

DAILY
The fitness industry, decoded — in five minutes.
Friday, 25 September 2026 · Weekday
The members you think quit might just have a declined card — and that's actually great news.
— Sqwod
Money movement
⇄  Acquired
Jamieson Wellness
 C$45.75/share

Connect the dots
Churn or billing glitch? The answer changes everything.
There's a quiet disaster hiding in most studio dashboards: a failed payment triggers a lapse, the system logs a cancellation, and an operator spends the next quarter blaming their programming. But the member never actually wanted to leave — their card expired. That's not a retention problem; that's a collections problem, and those are much easier to fix.
The practical upshot: before you redesign your onboarding, slash prices, or panic-hire a community manager, pull your last 90 days of involuntary churn and see how many exits trace back to billing failures. If your payment recovery flow is a single automated email, you're leaving real members — and real revenue — on the table. A dunning sequence with 3–5 touches (email, SMS, in-app) can claw back a meaningful slice of what you assumed was lost.
The rundown
01
The Churn Problem Hiding in Your Failed Payments
Athletech News flags a sneaky revenue leak operators often misread as cancellations: failed payments quietly pushing members out the door before anyone notices. Fix the billing, and you might find your retention numbers were better than you thought.
Source: Athletech News →
02
C$45.75/Share: Jamieson Wellness Heads to the Exit
Shareholders are voting on a full cash buyout of Jamieson Wellness at C$45.75 per share — a reminder that even the biggest names in the supplement aisle aren't immune to a quiet acquisition when the price is right.
Source: TradingView →
03
Google Fitbit Air Is Coming to India — Here's What We Know
Analytics Insight has the rundown on expected pricing, launch timing, and key features for Google's next Fitbit — and if wearables are part of how you sell or support your clients, this one's worth a spot on your radar.
Source: Analytics Insight →
04
$3.8B and counting: Australia's fitness industry is having a moment
Australasian Leisure Management Magazine forecasts Australian fitness industry revenue is closing in on $3.8 billion — which means the market is growing, and the operators who move now are the ones who'll be taking a bigger slice of it.
Source: Australasian Leisure Management Magazine →
05
Germany eyes the Olympics — and the fitness industry is all in
The DSSV is backing Germany's Olympic bid, framing the Games as a national nudge toward a more active population. For studio operators, that kind of top-down momentum for movement culture is exactly the tailwind worth paying attention to.
Source: DSSV →
06
UK Pilates Market Hits £1.1B — and Men Are Finally Showing Up
The UK Pilates industry has reached a £1.1 billion valuation, with male participation driving a chunk of that growth. If you haven't built a men's offer yet, the market just handed you a very expensive hint.
Source: streamlinefeed.co.ke →
Policy watch
Germany's Olympic bid gets the fitness industry's stamp of approval
The DSSV is formally backing Germany's Olympic bid, positioning the Games as a national catalyst for a more active population. For operators in Europe, government-level momentum behind movement culture can translate into subsidized memberships, employer wellness mandates, and new public-private partnership funding worth watching.
Stat
£1.1B
UK Pilates market valuation
A billion-pound market with male participation as the growth engine signals that Pilates is no longer a niche — operators without a men's offer are sitting out a demonstrably large and expanding segment.
Sqwod recs
✓ Track: Start separating 'voluntary churn' from 'involuntary churn' in your monthly reporting — most studio software can tag the difference, and the two problems require completely different fixes.
✓ Try: Run one men's-focused Pilates or mobility trial class with explicit positioning (strength, injury prevention, performance) — use it as a test-and-learn before committing to a full program rebuild.

DAILY
The fitness industry, decoded — in five minutes.
Wednesday, 23 September 2026 · Weekday
The gym floor is a policy document — and Cult Fitness just published a very loud edit.
— Sqwod
Money movement

Connect the dots
House rules are theatre until you enforce them publicly
When a Bengaluru member hurled 20-kg equipment and Cult Fitness cancelled their membership, the real product wasn't discipline — it was signal. Every other member watching (and the internet definitely watched) learned exactly where the line is. Most studios post rules on a laminated sheet and pray. The ones that enforce fast and visibly are building something more durable: a culture with actual teeth.
Here's the operator truth: your code of conduct is only as strong as the last time you acted on it. If your staff hesitated, escalated for thirty minutes, or quietly let it slide, you don't have a policy — you have a suggestion. Audit your incident protocol this week. Who has authority to act? What's the script? Because as the KPMG story proves, the internet will timestamp every second of your team's indecision and fundraise around it.
The rundown
01
DSSV takes fitness lobbying to the Reichstag steps
Germany's gym industry association staged a live workout outside parliament to put fitness policy on politicians' radar. If you've ever wanted proof that the sector is flexing its political muscle, this is it.
Source: DSSV →
02
Bird&Be Pulls in $13M to Put Male Fertility on the Map
The fertility brand just closed a $13M raise to bring male reproductive health into the mainstream conversation. For wellness operators, it's a signal that men's health is moving from niche to necessary — and that's a market worth watching.
Source: Athletech News →
03
20-kg wake-up call: Cult Fitness boots member who hurled equipment
A Bengaluru Cult Fitness member got their membership cancelled after throwing 20-kg equipment on the gym floor at Indiranagar — a reminder that your house rules are only as strong as your willingness to enforce them, fast and publicly.
Source: Hindustan Times →
04
Discover Strength Plants Its Flag in Massachusetts With Wellesley Studio
The evidence-based strength brand is making its Greater Boston debut — and for operators watching where growth-minded franchisors are placing their bets, the suburbs are clearly still very much in play.
Source: Health & Fitness Association →
05
Magic AI fitness mirror raises £8m to crack the US
The UK startup just secured £8m to take its AI-powered mirror stateside — which means the connected fitness hardware race is still very much on, and the market you're competing in just got a little more crowded.
Source: The Times →
06
$80K raised after KPMG manager fired over gym video
A GoFundMe for Yuen Lee — let go following a viral gym altercation clip — has cleared $80,000, a reminder that how staff handle conflict on the floor is now very much a public event. If your team doesn't have a clear incident protocol, the internet will write one for you.
Source: primetimer.com →
Policy watch
Germany's gym sector takes its case to parliament
DSSV staged a live workout outside the Reichstag to push fitness policy onto politicians' agendas — a sign that the European gym industry is done waiting for a seat at the table and is staging one outside. Operators elsewhere should take note: collective lobbying moves regulation faster than individual complaints.

✓ Steal: Borrow from hospitality: post your code of conduct at point of sale (signup, not just the wall) and have new members verbally confirm one key rule — it primes accountability before they ever set foot on the floor.
✓ Read: Look up 'psychological safety in high-performance environments' — the same research that shapes elite sports teams applies directly to how your coaches handle confrontation without freezing or overreacting.
